subject: Literature
title: Mary Shelley's Frankenstein as Proto-Dystopia
description: A 60-second lesson on Mary Shelley's Frankenstein as Proto-Dystopia.

hook.text: A teenage girl wrote Frankenstein during a ghost story contest and accidentally invented science fiction.

buildup.text: Mary Shelley was only eighteen when she created the story of a scientist who builds a creature and then abandons it.

discovery.text: Frankenstein is not really about a monster. It is about the catastrophe of creating without taking responsibility.

twist.text: The creature is articulate and philosophical, not a groaning brute. Hollywood rewrote Shelley's nuanced creation.

climax.text: Shelley established the template for all dystopian science fiction: technology without ethics leads to devastation.

punchline.text: A teenager warned the world about playing god. Nobody listened.

quiz.question: What is Frankenstein really about, beyond the surface horror?
options: The dangers of electricity and lightning
The catastrophe of creating without taking responsibility
